---
title: "SPARQL Property Paths"
format:
  html:
    code-fold: false
engine: julia

## Overview

SPARQL 1.1 property paths allow you to match chains of predicates in a single triple pattern. RDFLib.jl supports the full property path specification: sequence, alternative, inverse, repetition, and negation.

```{julia}
using RDFLib

# Build a graph with organizational and social relationships
g = RDFGraph()
ex = Namespace("http://example.org/")
foaf = Namespace("http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/")
bind!(g, "ex", ex)
bind!(g, "foaf", foaf)

# Organizational hierarchy: CEO → VP → Manager → Employee
add!(g, Triple(ex("ceo"), ex("manages"), ex("vp1")))
add!(g, Triple(ex("ceo"), ex("manages"), ex("vp2")))
add!(g, Triple(ex("vp1"), ex("manages"), ex("mgr1")))
add!(g, Triple(ex("vp2"), ex("manages"), ex("mgr2")))
add!(g, Triple(ex("mgr1"), ex("manages"), ex("emp1")))
add!(g, Triple(ex("mgr1"), ex("manages"), ex("emp2")))
add!(g, Triple(ex("mgr2"), ex("manages"), ex("emp3")))

# People with names and roles
for (person, name, role) in [
    ("ceo", "Alice", "CEO"), ("vp1", "Bob", "VP"),
    ("vp2", "Carol", "VP"), ("mgr1", "Dave", "Manager"),
    ("mgr2", "Eve", "Manager"), ("emp1", "Frank", "Employee"),
    ("emp2", "Grace", "Employee"), ("emp3", "Hank", "Employee")]
    add!(g, Triple(ex(person), foaf("name"), Literal(name)))
    add!(g, Triple(ex(person), ex("role"), Literal(role)))
end

# Social links
add!(g, Triple(ex("emp1"), foaf("knows"), ex("emp2")))
add!(g, Triple(ex("emp2"), foaf("knows"), ex("emp3")))
add!(g, Triple(ex("emp1"), ex("worksIn"), ex("engineering")))
add!(g, Triple(ex("emp2"), ex("worksIn"), ex("engineering")))
add!(g, Triple(ex("emp3"), ex("worksIn"), ex("marketing")))
add!(g, Triple(ex("engineering"), ex("partOf"), ex("tech_division")))
add!(g, Triple(ex("marketing"), ex("partOf"), ex("business_division")))

println("Graph has $(length(g)) triples")
```

## Sequence Paths (/)

A sequence path matches a chain of predicates. `ex:manages/ex:manages` matches two hops.

```{julia}
# Who does the CEO manage through exactly two levels?
results = sparql_query(g, """
    PREFIX ex: <http://example.org/>
    SELECT ?person ?name WHERE {
        ex:ceo ex:manages/ex:manages ?person .
        ?person <http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/name> ?name .
    }
""")
println("CEO's skip-level reports:")
for row in results
    println("  ", row[:name])
end
```

```{julia}
# Three-level chain: CEO → VP → Manager → Employee
results = sparql_query(g, """
    PREFIX ex: <http://example.org/>
    PREFIX foaf: <http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/>
    SELECT ?name WHERE {
        ex:ceo ex:manages/ex:manages/ex:manages ?emp .
        ?emp foaf:name ?name .
    }
""")
println("CEO's 3rd-level reports:")
for row in results
    println("  ", row[:name])
end
```

## Alternative Paths (|)

Match either of two predicates.

```{julia}
# Find connections via either manages or knows
results = sparql_query(g, """
    PREFIX ex: <http://example.org/>
    PREFIX foaf: <http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/>
    SELECT ?a ?b WHERE {
        ?a (ex:manages|foaf:knows) ?b .
    }
""")
println("Management or social links: $(length(results)) pairs")
for row in results
    println("  ", row[:a], " → ", row[:b])
end
```

## Inverse Paths (^)

Traverse a predicate in the reverse direction.

```{julia}
# Who manages emp1? (inverse of manages)
results = sparql_query(g, """
    PREFIX ex: <http://example.org/>
    PREFIX foaf: <http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/>
    SELECT ?manager ?name WHERE {
        ex:emp1 ^ex:manages ?manager .
        ?manager foaf:name ?name .
    }
""")
println("emp1's manager:")
for row in results
    println("  ", row[:name])
end
```

```{julia}
# Inverse in a sequence: who manages someone who manages emp1?
results = sparql_query(g, """
    PREFIX ex: <http://example.org/>
    PREFIX foaf: <http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/>
    SELECT ?name WHERE {
        ex:emp1 ^ex:manages/^ex:manages ?boss .
        ?boss foaf:name ?name .
    }
""")
println("emp1's boss's boss:")
for row in results
    println("  ", row[:name])
end
```

## Transitive Closure — ZeroOrMore (*) and OneOrMore (+)

Repeat a predicate zero-or-more or one-or-more times.

```{julia}
# OneOrMore (+): all people the CEO manages at ANY level (transitive closure)
results = sparql_query(g, """
    PREFIX ex: <http://example.org/>
    PREFIX foaf: <http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/>
    SELECT ?person ?name WHERE {
        ex:ceo ex:manages+ ?person .
        ?person foaf:name ?name .
    }
""")
println("All reports under CEO (transitive):")
for row in results
    println("  ", row[:name])
end
```

```{julia}
# ZeroOrMore (*): includes the starting node itself
results = sparql_query(g, """
    PREFIX ex: <http://example.org/>
    SELECT ?person WHERE {
        ex:mgr1 ex:manages* ?person .
    }
""")
println("mgr1 and all below (zero-or-more):")
for row in results
    println("  ", row[:person])
end
```

## ZeroOrOne (?)

Match zero or one occurrence — the target may be the start node or one hop away.

```{julia}
# emp1 or anyone emp1 directly knows
results = sparql_query(g, """
    PREFIX foaf: <http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/>
    PREFIX ex: <http://example.org/>
    SELECT ?person WHERE {
        ex:emp1 foaf:knows? ?person .
    }
""")
println("emp1 and immediate acquaintances:")
for row in results
    println("  ", row[:person])
end
```

## Negated Property Sets (!)

Match any predicate EXCEPT the listed ones.

```{julia}
# Find triples about emp1 with any predicate except rdf:type and foaf:name
results = sparql_query(g, """
    PREFIX ex: <http://example.org/>
    PREFIX foaf: <http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/>
    SELECT ?p ?o WHERE {
        ex:emp1 !(rdf:type|foaf:name) ?o .
        ex:emp1 ?p ?o .
    }
""")
println("emp1 facts (excluding type and name):")
for row in results
    println("  ", row[:p], " → ", row[:o])
end
```

## Complex Path Expressions

Combine path operators for sophisticated traversals.

```{julia}
# Reachability: find everyone connected to emp1 via knows (in either direction)
results = sparql_query(g, """
    PREFIX foaf: <http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/>
    PREFIX ex: <http://example.org/>
    SELECT ?person WHERE {
        ex:emp1 (foaf:knows|^foaf:knows)+ ?person .
    }
""")
println("Social network of emp1 (bidirectional):")
for row in results
    println("  ", row[:person])
end
```

```{julia}
# Sequence + transitive: what division does emp1 belong to?
# emp1 → worksIn → department → partOf* → division
results = sparql_query(g, """
    PREFIX ex: <http://example.org/>
    SELECT ?org WHERE {
        ex:emp1 ex:worksIn/ex:partOf* ?org .
    }
""")
println("emp1's organizational chain:")
for row in results
    println("  ", row[:org])
end
```

## Practical Example: Class Hierarchy

Property paths excel at traversing RDF Schema and OWL class hierarchies.

```{julia}
# Build a class hierarchy
h = RDFGraph()
ex = Namespace("http://example.org/")
bind!(h, "ex", ex)

add!(h, Triple(ex("Dog"), RDFS("subClassOf"), ex("Mammal")))
add!(h, Triple(ex("Mammal"), RDFS("subClassOf"), ex("Animal")))
add!(h, Triple(ex("Animal"), RDFS("subClassOf"), ex("LivingThing")))
add!(h, Triple(ex("Cat"), RDFS("subClassOf"), ex("Mammal")))
add!(h, Triple(ex("Parrot"), RDFS("subClassOf"), ex("Bird")))
add!(h, Triple(ex("Bird"), RDFS("subClassOf"), ex("Animal")))

# Find all superclasses of Dog
results = sparql_query(h, """
    PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>
    PREFIX ex: <http://example.org/>
    SELECT ?class WHERE {
        ex:Dog rdfs:subClassOf+ ?class .
    }
""")
println("Dog is a subclass of:")
for row in results
    println("  ", row[:class])
end
```

```{julia}
# Find all subclasses of Animal (inverse transitive)
results = sparql_query(h, """
    PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>
    PREFIX ex: <http://example.org/>
    SELECT ?class WHERE {
        ?class rdfs:subClassOf+ ex:Animal .
    }
""")
println("Subclasses of Animal:")
for row in results
    println("  ", row[:class])
end
```

## Using Paths with ASK and CONSTRUCT

Property paths work with all SPARQL query forms.

```{julia}
# ASK: is Dog a (transitive) subclass of LivingThing?
result = sparql_query(h, """
    PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>
    PREFIX ex: <http://example.org/>
    ASK { ex:Dog rdfs:subClassOf+ ex:LivingThing }
""")
println("Dog subClassOf+ LivingThing? ", result)
```

```{julia}
# CONSTRUCT: materialize the transitive closure
result = sparql_query(h, """
    PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>
    PREFIX ex: <http://example.org/>
    CONSTRUCT { ?sub ex:isKindOf ?super }
    WHERE { ?sub rdfs:subClassOf+ ?super }
""")
println("Materialized $(length(result)) transitive subclass triples")
for t in triples(result, (nothing, nothing, nothing))
    println("  ", t.subject, " isKindOf ", t.object)
end
```

## Summary

| Syntax | Name | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `p/q` | Sequence | Match p then q |
| `p\|q` | Alternative | Match p or q |
| `^p` | Inverse | Traverse p backwards |
| `p*` | ZeroOrMore | 0+ hops (includes start) |
| `p+` | OneOrMore | 1+ hops (transitive closure) |
| `p?` | ZeroOrOne | Optional single hop |
| `!(p\|q)` | Negated set | Any predicate except p, q |
